The impact of maternal cardiovascular risk factors and diseases on offspring cardiovascular health.
items.abstract: The increasing number of pregnancies among women at cardiovascular risk or with established cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) has become a major global health concern because of its lasting influence on the health of their offspring. Maternal heart disease, hypertension, diabetes, obesity, and abnormal lipid levels, including also elevated lipoprotein(a), can disturb fetal growth and development, leading to changes in the heart, blood vessels, and metabolism that raise the risk of CVD problems in childhood and later life. The rising age of pregnant women, especially in the developed countries, also increases this risk. These effects result from a combination of inherited traits and alterations in the intrauterine environment, including impaired blood flow, inflammation, oxidative stress, and disrupted nutrient transfer through the placenta. Such disturbances can modify the structure and function of the developing cardiovascular system and contribute to lifelong vulnerability to CVDs. Studies from large populations show that children born to mothers with cardiovascular conditions have about twice the risk of developing CVD compared with those born to healthy mothers. Good maternal health before and during pregnancy, supported by balanced nutrition, regular physical activity, and effective control of blood pressure, lipids, body weight, and blood sugar, is strongly linked to better outcomes for both mother and child. Although current lifestyle interventions in pregnancy have shown promising effects on maternal wellbeing, their influence on the long-term cardiovascular health of the offspring remains uncertain. Strengthening preconception care, well-designed healthcare education, improving cardiovascular screening in women of reproductive age, and promoting heart-healthy habits across the life course are essential to prevent the transfer of cardiovascular risk from one generation to the next.

Sex-disaggregated Outcomes and Safety Reporting in Perioperative Systemic Therapy for Muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Sex may influence patients' response to chemotherapy or immunotherapy given before or after radical cystectomy. We reviewed all otherwise eligible prospective perioperative interventional studies, including randomized controlled trials and single-arm studies, to determine how often female enrollment, efficacy outcomes, and safety outcomes were reported separately for women and men. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched for phase 1-3 prospective interventional studies, including randomized controlled trials and single-arm studies, evaluating perioperative systemic therapy for nonmetastatic muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) between 1990 and 2024. Eligibility was based on disease setting, perioperative intervention, prospective design, and full-text availability; reporting of sex-specific outcomes was not required for inclusion and was instead coded as a review outcome. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted female enrollment and published sex-stratified efficacy or safety outcomes, and assessed risk of bias using design-appropriate tools. Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 was applied to randomized trials and the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS) to noncomparative single-arm studies. Outcomes of interest were the proportion of studies reporting efficacy or adverse events (AEs) by sex, the proportion reporting formal sex-by-treatment interaction tests, and the sex-specific hazard ratios (HRs), response rates, or survival estimates provided. Twenty-nine reports of 27 unique prospective perioperative trials were included, comprising 21 neoadjuvant and eight adjuvant reports, covering 6376 patients; 1140 (18%) were women. Female enrollment was 17% in neoadjuvant chemotherapy trials, 17% in neoadjuvant immunotherapy trials, 17% in adjuvant chemotherapy trials, and 22% in adjuvant immunotherapy trials. Five reports (17%) reported any sex-disaggregated efficacy outcome, whereas none reported AEs by sex. The pooled Nordic neoadjuvant series reported a female-versus-male HR >1 for overall survival (HR 1.36, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.97-1.92), although the estimate was imprecise. PURE-01 reported an imprecise female-versus-male event-free survival estimate (HR 1.15, 95% CI 0.44-3.00). In the adjuvant setting, individual cisplatin-based trials provided limited and mostly descriptive sex-specific information, whereas CheckMate-274 nivolumab reported disease-free survival estimates for women (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.38-1.06) and men (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.52-0.83), with the reported interaction test not providing clear evidence of heterogeneity (p = 0.58). Among randomized trials, risk of bias was low in eight reports, raised some concerns in eight, and was high in one; single-arm studies scored 12-15 of 16 on MINORS. Reliance on published summaries, limited female representation, and heterogeneous study designs limited formal inference. Women remain underrepresented in perioperative MIBC trials and are absent from safety reporting. The available evidence is insufficient to determine whether clinically meaningful sex-based differences in benefit exist, and modest sex-based differences cannot be excluded. Future trials should ensure balanced recruitment, stratify randomization by sex when randomization is used, and report disaggregated efficacy and toxicity outcomes to support equitable care.

Zanidatamab in the treatment of esophagogastric adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract: Esophagogastric cancer (EGC) remains a leading cause of cancer‑related mortality worldwide. Approximately 15-20% of advanced EGC overexpress human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2). Since 2010, trastuzumab in combination with platinum and fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy has been the cornerstone of first-line therapy for HER2-positive advanced EGC, with a modest overall survival benefit. The addition of pembrolizumab to trastuzumab and chemotherapy in the KEYNOTE-811 trial has improved outcomes in PD-L1‑positive tumors. Despite these advances, median overall survival remains below 20 months. Zanidatamab is a novel biparatopic HER2-directed antibody, designed to bind to two distinct extracellular domains of HER2, promoting receptor clustering, enhanced internalization, and immune-mediated cytotoxicity. This Drug Evaluation reviews the pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, clinical development, efficacy, safety, and regulatory status of zanidatamab in HER2-positive EGC. The phase III HERIZON-GEA-01 trial evaluated zanidatamab (with or without tislelizumab) plus chemotherapy as first-line treatment for HER2-positive advanced EGC. This trial demonstrated clinically meaningful improvements in progression-free and overall survival versus trastuzumab-based therapy, leading to FDA approval of zanidatamab plus chemotherapy, with or without tislelizumab, as first‑line treatment for HER2-positive unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric, gastroesophageal junction, or esophageal adenocarcinoma. Key questions remain regarding optimal patient selection, the role of tislelizumab across PD-L1 subgroups, sequencing with antibody-drug conjugates, and long-term safety. Cancers of the esophagus, stomach, and the junction between the stomach and the food pipe, known as esophagogastric cancer, are common globally and often have poor outcomes. About one in five of these cancers has a protein called HER2 on the surface of cancer cells. For over 15 years, trastuzumab, a drug that blocks HER2, when given with chemotherapy, has been the standard treatment for these patients. Zanidatamab is a new treatment that works by attaching to two different parts of two neighboring HER2 proteins at the same time by linking them side-by-side. This may block cancer growth more effectively than trastuzumab. A large clinical trial called HERIZON-GEA-01 tested zanidatamab combined with chemotherapy, with or without another immune system drug called tislelizumab, against standard trastuzumab plus chemotherapy as the first treatment for patients with HER2-positive spread cancer that started in the esophagus, stomach, or the junction between the stomach and the food pipe. This trial showed that patients receiving zanidatamab and chemotherapy with or without immunotherapy lived significantly longer than those receiving standard trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. Side effects were generally manageable, with diarrhea being the most notable additional side effect compared to trastuzumab. Based on these results, the FDA approved both zanidatamab-based combinations in August 2026 as a new first-line treatment option, replacing trastuzumab as the preferred HER2-targeted treatment for this type of cancer.

Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma with METex14 mutation and high PD-L1: A case report.
items.abstract: Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC) is a rare and aggressive subtype of lung cancer, posing diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Cases of PSC harboring both MET exon 14 skipping (METex14) mutation and high PD-L1 expression are rarely documented, and reports detailing multimodal treatment involving surgery, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy in such patients are even scarcer. A 54-year-old man presented with a persistent cough for over half a month. He was previously healthy. Physical examination revealed diminished breath sounds in the right upper lung. Initial bronchoscopic biopsy suggested inflammation, and computed tomography (CT)-guided lung biopsy showed atypical giant cells but was inconclusive. Following multidisciplinary team discussion, the patient underwent surgical resection. Postoperative pathology confirmed pleomorphic carcinoma (sarcomatoid carcinoma). Subsequent genetic testing identified a METex14 mutation with high PD-L1 expression (Tumor Proportion Score ≥ 50%). The final diagnosis was stage IIIB (T4N2M0) right PSC, MET-positive, PD-L1-positive. The initial treatment plan included 1 cycle of toripalimab (an anti-PD-1 antibody) combined with docetaxel and lobaplatin chemotherapy. This was subsequently adjusted to boretinib (a MET inhibitor) targeted therapy combined with docetaxel and lobaplatin chemotherapy. The patient achieved and maintained a partial response (PR) for over 6 months of follow-up. Symptoms including cough resolved, and his general condition remained good with satisfactory appetite and sleep. This case underscores the diagnostic difficulty of PSC, which is prone to misdiagnosis and exhibits rapid growth. Surgery may not be appropriate for unresectable stage IIIB PSC. Gene sequencing and PD-L1 testing are crucial as they expand therapeutic options for PSC patients. The optimal first-line therapy (targeted vs immunotherapy) for PSC with concurrent MET mutation and high PD-L1 expression remains undefined, warranting further exploration of combination strategies.

items.title: Synchronous hepatocellular carcinoma and nasopharyngeal carcinoma in a patient with chronic hepatitis B: A case report and literature review.
items.abstract: Synchronous double primary cancers involving hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) are exceptionally rare. Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is an established cause of HCC, whereas Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is the major etiological factor for NPC. We report a patient with synchronous HCC and NPC and review the relevant literature. A 63-year-old Chinese man with chronic HBV presented with a liver mass detected on routine screening. He reported nasal obstruction. Contrast-enhanced imaging showed a 46 × 59 mm hepatic lesion with portal vein tumor thrombus and a 41 × 29 mm nasopharyngeal mass with bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. Biopsies confirmed moderately differentiated HCC and EBV-associated non-keratinizing NPC. Final diagnoses were HCC Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer Stage C (CNLC IIIa, Child-Pugh A) and NPC T3N2M0 Stage III (AJCC 8th edition). He received hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC, mFOLFOX) combined with tislelizumab and donafenib; radiotherapy for NPC was deferred after shared decision-making. Entecavir was continued. At 19-month follow-up, both tumors remained controlled; the NPC met radiographic complete response criteria. Synchronous HCC and EBV-associated NPC were controlled during treatment with a tislelizumab-containing multimodality regimen, and the NPC achieved a radiographic complete response. The contribution of each treatment component cannot be determined from a single case, and definitive radiotherapy remains the standard of care for locoregionally advanced NPC. Multidisciplinary management and close monitoring are essential.

items.title: Association between prior HBV vaccine responsiveness and booster-induced anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike antibody titers following the third BNT162b2 dose in Japanese healthcare workers: A prospective observational study.
items.abstract: Inter-individual variability in vaccine-induced humoral responses has been reported even among generally healthy individuals. In our previous study, healthcare workers with poor hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccine responsiveness were more likely to show a low anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike antibody response after the first BNT162b2 dose. This study examined whether such differences persisted after a third BNT162b2 dose. This was an extended follow-up study of a previously reported prospective observational cohort of Japanese healthcare workers. The primary outcome was the quantitative anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike antibody titer measured 12 weeks after the third BNT162b2 dose. Participants were classified as normal HBV vaccine responders, weak responders, or non-responders. Comparisons across HBV response groups were performed using the Kruskal-Wallis test and multivariable linear regression adjusted for age and sex. A low antibody-response analysis (<15 U/mL) after the first dose was evaluated as a secondary analysis. Among 741 participants with antibody measurements 12 weeks after the third dose, 486 were normal HBV vaccine responders, 229 were weak responders, and 26 were non-responders. The median anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike antibody titer was 891,900 U/mL. Titers did not differ significantly across HBV response groups in the unadjusted analysis (P = .3718) or after adjustment for age and sex (global P = .3971). Compared with normal responders, the adjusted geometric mean ratio was 0.94 (95% CI, 0.83-1.07) for weak responders and 0.83 (95% CI, 0.60-1.15) for non-responders. By contrast, after the first dose, HBV vaccine non-responders had an increased risk of a low antibody response (<15 U/mL) compared with normal responders (adjusted RR, 1.85; 95% CI, 1.10-3.13). Differences in early anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike antibody responses associated with prior HBV vaccine responsiveness were no longer statistically apparent 12 weeks after the third BNT162b2 dose. These findings suggest convergence of measured humoral antibody responses after booster vaccination, although they do not establish that the underlying biological mechanisms of vaccine hyporesponsiveness were eliminated.

Cytokine release syndrome across three immunotherapy platforms: A real-world patient-level comparison of CAR T-cell, T-cell engager, and immune checkpoint inhibitor therapies.
items.abstract: Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) may represent a spectrum of treatment-specific phenotypes rather than a uniform clinical entity. To our knowledge, this is the first real-world patient-level comparison of CRS following chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T), T-cell engager (TCE), and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. CRS cases after CAR-T, TCE (tebentafusp/brenetafusp), or ICI therapy in the SERIO-registry were compared regarding presentation, additional toxicities, management, and tumor outcomes. Among 1765 patients registered in SERIO, CRS was documented in 189/213 CAR-T recipients (88.7%), 57/90 TCE recipients (63.3%), and 9/1378 ICI recipients (0.7%). Of those who developed CRS, grade ≥ 3 CRS occurred in 11% of CAR-T and 4% of TCE recipients, but in none of the nine ICI-associated cases. Median onset was 2.5, < 1, and 21.5 days after CAR-T, TCE, and ICI, respectively. Tocilizumab use varied (90%, 4%, and 11%, respectively; CAR-T vs TCE, p < 0.001). Additional treatment-related toxicities affected 43%, 14%, and 56% of CAR-T, TCE, and ICI recipients, respectively (CAR-T vs TCE, p < 0.001; ICI vs TCE, p = 0.034), with distinct patterns: immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) predominated after CAR-T, cutaneous toxicities after TCE, and hepatitis or thyroiditis after ICI. CRS resolved in 99-100%; one CRS-related death followed CAR-T. No statistically significant association between CRS occurrence or severity and tumor response was detected. CRS is not a uniform toxicity, with differences in onset, severity, management, and additional toxicities observed across CAR-T, TCE, and ICI treatment settings. These findings highlight the importance of treatment context in CRS assessment and management.

items.title: Commonly expressed key driver genes in the pathogenesis of viral and non-viral liver cancer.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a common and lethal liver cancer primarily associated with viral infections like hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV), as well as non-viral causes. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of these subtypes is essential for identifying potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In this study, an integrated bioinformatics approach was used to analyze publicly available datasets related to HBV-associated, HCV-associated, and non-viral HCC. Functional enrichment analyses and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed to identify key hub genes. Our analysis identified dysregulated genes across all HCC subtypes. Among these, GPC3 and SPARCL1 were significantly upregulated, while ALB and HNF4α were downregulated, and are involved in critical cancer pathways such as Wnt, PI3K/Akt, and p53 signaling. Functional analysis linked these DEGs to essential processes in tumorigenesis, including cell cycle regulation and immune modulation. Notably, SPARCL1 has been identified as a potential inhibitor of SPP1, a key driver of HCC. Validation using databases such as GEPIA and TNMplot confirmed the dysregulation of these genes in numerous HCC tissue samples and their significant association with patient prognosis. This study provides a comprehensive overview of HCC pathogenesis by suggesting a shared gene profile between viral and non-viral forms, paving the way for universal diagnostic markers and targeted therapies while highlighting the need for further experimental validation to advance precision medicine in HCC.

items.title: Primary splenic angiosarcoma initially diagnosed as littoral cell angioma: A case report of a diagnostic pitfall.
items.abstract: Primary splenic angiosarcoma (PSAn) is a rare and aggressive vascular malignancy that poses diagnostic challenges because of its overlapping morphological and immunohistochemical features with benign splenic vascular tumors. A 71-year-old woman presented with left upper abdominal pain, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, and a splenic lesion. Splenectomy and excision of a separate 1-cm hepatic nodule were performed, with initial pathological diagnoses of splenic littoral cell angioma and hepatic cavernous hemangioma. Persistent postoperative fever, progressive cytopenias, jaundice, hepatic dysfunction, and newly developed diffuse multifocal hepatic lesions subsequently occurred. Pathological reevaluation of the splenic specimen using an expanded immunohistochemical panel resulted in a revised diagnosis of PSAn. The subsequently developed diffuse hepatic lesions were considered highly suspicious for hepatic metastases based on the radiological and clinical findings, although histological confirmation was unavailable. The patient underwent splenectomy and excision of the initial hepatic nodule. Multidisciplinary reassessment and pathological reevaluation were performed following clinical deterioration. The patient declined liver biopsy and further oncological treatment. Despite supportive management, the patient's condition progressively deteriorated. She was discharged after 2 weeks and died 2 months later. PSAn should be considered in the differential diagnosis of splenic vascular tumors, particularly when morphological and immunohistochemical findings overlap. Unexpected postoperative deterioration should prompt timely multidisciplinary reassessment and pathological review.

items.title: Effects and safety of Korean red ginseng on the clinical course of uterine leiomyoma: A double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial.
items.abstract: Korean red ginseng (KRG) is widely used as a dietary supplement, but its effects on uterine leiomyoma growth and reproductive hormones are unclear. We evaluated whether KRG affects leiomyoma growth, routine laboratory indices, or endocrine profiles in premenopausal women with uterine leiomyoma managed expectantly. In this single-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial, premenopausal women aged 20 to 45 years with a uterine leiomyoma of 1 to 8 cm suitable for expectant management were allocated 1:1 to KRG 3 g/d or matching placebo for 6 months. Participants, investigators, ultrasonography examiners, and analysts were blinded. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the 6-month change in maximal diameter of the index leiomyoma on ultrasonography, analyzed by analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline diameter. Secondary outcomes were complete blood count, ferritin, liver enzymes, and reproductive hormones. Between December 2015 and September 2019, 69 participants were randomized (placebo 34, KRG 35) and 61 completed the 6-month assessment (placebo 30, KRG 31); all 8 noncompletions were losses to follow-up. Maximal diameter increased modestly in both groups, with no significant between-group difference in change (mean difference -0.11 cm; 95% confidence interval: -0.33 to 0.12; P = .34); the upper confidence limit lay below the prespecified target difference of 0.33 cm. There were no significant between-group differences in laboratory changes or in baseline-, age-, and body mass index-adjusted log scale hormone ratios, and the multivariate hormone profile did not differ between groups (Pillai's trace = 0.056; P = .68). In exploratory post hoc analyses, the internal correlation structure among hormone changes was similar in both arms. No treatment-related serious adverse event and no discontinuation for intolerance was documented, although adverse events were ascertained passively. In premenopausal women with uterine leiomyoma managed expectantly, 6 months of KRG supplementation did not meaningfully alter leiomyoma growth, routine laboratory indices, or reproductive hormone homeostasis compared with placebo. Within the constraints of a modest sample size, incomplete characterization of the study product, and passive adverse-event ascertainment, these findings do not establish the safety of KRG, and they support no conclusion regarding nonserious adverse effects.

items.title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Sudden Cardiac Death: Epidemiology, Mechanisms, Risk Stratification, and Prevention.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most prevalent chronic metabolic liver disease worldwide. Cardiovascular adverse events have long been the leading cause of death in the MASLD population, far exceeding liver-related mortality. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) represents the most insidious and rapidly progressing extreme clinical phenotype among these cardiovascular complications. However, the relationship between MASLD and SCD has long received insufficient attention. Accumulating evidence from clinical studies indicates that MASLD is associated with elevated sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) risk independent of conventional cardiometabolic risk factors. Notably, while non-invasive clinical proxies of hepatic steatosis (such as the fatty liver index) identify individuals with heightened susceptibility to SCA, advancing liver fibrosis shows the strongest, gradient-dependent association with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, although its relation to SCA or SCD specifically requires confirmation. Sudden death in MASLD may result from primary ventricular arrhythmias or, in advanced cirrhosis, from non-shockable arrest due to hemodynamic, infectious, or metabolic decompensation. Although shared cardiometabolic risk factors account for a substantial portion of this association, proposed mechanisms include insulin resistance-related myocardial energy disturbances, inflammation-associated myocardial and electrophysiological remodeling, cirrhosis-associated circulatory dysfunction, and gut-derived endotoxemia. In clinical practice, non-invasive fibrosis scores, circulating biomarkers, and imaging parameters represent promising candidate risk markers for evaluating electrophysiological vulnerability, though a validated, MASLD-specific SCD risk prediction model remains to be established. Strategies such as lifestyle intervention, metabolic-targeted pharmacotherapy, and intensive management of cardiovascular risk factors may interrupt the progression from MASLD to SCD. This review summarizes the current evidence to inform cardiovascular risk management across the course of MASLD.

items.title: Sorcin phase separation restrains p53 translation via stress granules to prevent hepatic stellate cell senescence in liver fibrosis.
items.abstract: Liver fibrosis (LF) is a dynamic process characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition driven by hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation. Inducing senescence in activated HSCs can limit fibrosis. The p53-p21 signaling axis is a key regulator of cellular senescence, however, how p53 activity is precisely controlled remains undefined. Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) has emerged as an important stress-adaptive regulatory mechanism, driving the formation of stress granules (SGs) that regulate mRNA fate. Here, integrative analyses of human and murine datasets revealed that Sorcin expression is upregulated during fibrosis progression. Functional studies showed that Sorcin suppresses HSC senescence, as evidenced by reduced senescence markers, decreased SA-β-Gal positivity, and enhanced proliferative capacity. Mechanistically, elevated intracellular calcium drives Sorcin-mediated LLPS, enabling cooperation with the RNA-binding protein TIAR to nucleate SGs-like condensates. RNA immunoprecipitation, polysome profiling, dual-luciferase assays and EMSA demonstrated that TIAR directly binds TP53 mRNA and represses its translation. Consequently, TP53 mRNA is sequestered within SG-like condensates, attenuating p53 signaling and delaying HSC senescence. In vivo, AAV-mediated Sorcin knockdown enhances HSC senescence and alleviates LF in a CCl 4 -induced mouse model. This study reveals a phase separation-mediated translational control mechanism governing HSC senescence. By restraining senescence, Sorcin sustains fibrotic persistence, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for LF.
